faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.

faqs.question: How do I change the font size of text when I print from software in Windows?
faqs.answer: You need to select the text or font size in the software you are printing from, not the printer driver. For detailed instructions, contact the company for the application you are printing from.

faqs.question: My product is out of color ink even though I print in black only. Why does this happen?
faqs.answer:
To keep the print head clear, the printer uses a small amount of ink from all the cartridges whenever it prints. Even if you select
Black Only
, some color ink is still being used.

faqs.question: I am unable to connect my product to a wireless network. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The printer does not come with built-in wireless features and does not support a wireless (or Ethernet) connection to a network router. Only a direct wired connection to the computer is supported.

faqs.question: I can't scan multiple document pages into a single PDF. What should I do?
faqs.answer: If you are using the Scanner Driver and Epson Scan Utility v2.92a or earlier, the ability to scan multiple pages to a single PDF is not supported. This feature is supported when using the Scanner Driver (which is sometimes shown as TWAIN Driver) and Epson Scan Utility v3.04a or higher. Check your product's Downloads tab to make sure you're using the latest version.

faqs.question: Does OS X support manual duplex printing with my product?
faqs.answer: This feature is not supported in Mac OS X. However, if your printer has a built-in automatic duplexer, auto-duplexing is supported in Mac OS X 10.6 (Snow Leopard).

faqs.question: My product makes noise after I turn it on or after it has been sitting for a while. What should I do?
faqs.answer: This is normal. It is performing routine maintenance.

faqs.question: I'm having paper feed problems. What should I do?
faqs.answer: If your EPSON Stylus Scan doesn't feed paper, feeds multiple pages, or paper is jammed, removed the jammed paper, then remove and replace the stack of paper. Finally, press the load/eject button. Make sure of the following: Paper isn't old, creased, damp, or too thin. Avoid humid environments. The edge guide is resting against the stack of paper. Paper isn't loaded above the arrow on the edge guide. If paper doesn't eject fully, you may have set the wrong paper size. Press the load/eject button to eject the paper. Then make sure you select the correct paper size in your application or print settings. Fan the stack of paper and then even the edges before loading it. Make sure your EPSON Stylus Scan is on a stable, level surface.

faqs.question: Does OS X support manual duplex printing with my product?
faqs.answer: This feature is not supported in Mac OS X. However, if your printer has a built-in automatic duplexer, auto-duplexing is supported in Mac OS X 10.6 (Snow Leopard).

faqs.question: My product sounds as though it is printing, but nothing prints. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure the print head nozzles are not clogged. To run a cleaning cycle, see "Cleaning the Print Head" on page 129 of your user's manual.

faqs.question: My printout has lines running through it. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure the print head nozzles are not clogged. Make sure the Media Type setting matches the paper you loaded. See "Choosing the Right Settings for EPSON Papers" on page 52 of your user's manual for guidelines. Make sure the printable side of the paper is face up. It's usually whiter or shinier. Enable Microweave and slide the Quality/Speed button to the Quality setting in printer setup. Check the LCD status display panel for a message that you're low on ink; see "Removing and Installing Ink Cartridges" on page 126. If your ink cartridge is more than six months old, you may need to replace it; see "Replacing an Outdated Ink Cartridge" on page 128 of your user's manual. If you see banding when you print, but not when you copy, try using Automatic mode. Make sure you're not using the Maximum Printable Area setting. Banding may occur in the expanded area: Set the paper thickness switch to the 0 position. Place the EPSON Stylus Scan on a stable, level surface. Make sure none of the five rubber feet is missing from the bottom of the EPSON Stylus Scan. Note: For other image quality problems when you're copying, see "Solving Image Quality Problems" beginning on page 151 of your user's manual.

faqs.question: My printout is blurry or smeared. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure your paper isn't damp, curled, or loaded face down (the printable side should be loaded face up). Try using Automatic mode. Use a support sheet with special paper or film, or try loading it one sheet at a time. Run the Print Head Alignment utility. Make sure the print head nozzles are not clogged. If you're using the automatic document feeder, try cleaning the paper path guide. Follow the instructions in "Cleaning the Paper Path Guide" on page 121 of your user's manual. Check the paper thickness switch position. If it's in the + position, your printer is set for thicker paper or envelopes and your image may smear. For most papers, set the paper thickness switch to the 0 position. Make sure your Media Type setting matches the paper you're using. See "Choosing the Right Settings for EPSON Papers" on page 52 of your user's manual for guidelines. For the best printouts, use EPSON papers and other media.

faqs.question: My printout is grainy when I print from any application. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Try using a higher quality paper. Run the Print Head Alignment utility. You may need to increase the image resolution or print it in a smaller size. See your software documentation for instructions. Set the monitor's color depth to at least 16-bit (24-bit is recommended).

faqs.question: The printout is faint or has gaps. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure the print head nozzles are not clogged. Check the LCD status display panel for a message that you're low on ink; see "Replacing an Ink Cartridge" on page 125 of your user's manual. Make sure the Media Type setting matches the paper you're using. Make sure your paper isn't damaged, old, dirty, or loaded face down. Try using Automatic mode.

faqs.question: My printout has incorrect or missing colors. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure the Ink setting is set to Color for color images. Make sure the print head nozzles are not clogged. If you are printing a high-resolution image, try turning off PhotoEnhance. Try using Automatic mode. See "Basic Printing with Windows" on page 43 of your user's manual or "Basic Printing on a Macintosh" on page 46 for instructions.

faqs.question: Why are my color documents printing in black and white?
faqs.answer: Make sure your EPSON Stylus Scan printer and software are selected in your software application. Make sure color printing is selected in your application and the printer software.

faqs.question: My product is printing blank pages from Windows or my Mac. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure the EPSON Stylus Scan 2500 Pro is selected in your application. Also, if you're running Windows, make sure it's selected as the Windows default printer. If you have a Macintosh, select SS 2500 in the Chooser. Make sure you have selected the correct paper size. Make sure the print head nozzles are not clogged.

faqs.question: The printout has a slight slant. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure the original document is positioned so that the horizontal and vertical edges are carefully aligned with the scales along the sides of the document table. If you're using the automatic document feeder, make sure the document guides fit snugly against the edges of the original document. If you're using EPSON Smart Panel's Copy Utility (Windows), select Straighten Only in the Automatic Photo Layout box.

faqs.question: Something is missing or incorrect in the image. What should I do?
faqs.answer: If your page is blank, make sure you place the original document face down on the document table. If you're using the automatic document feeder, make sure you load the document face up in the feeder. If text is missing or incorrect in your scanned image, try using the TWAIN software to adjust the threshold. See your electronic EPSON Stylus Scan 2500 Pro Reference Guide for more information. If your original document contains both text and graphics, text may not be recognized correctly by the OCR software. If you're using the TWAIN software, make sure you select the Quality & De-screening setting.

faqs.question: The image quality is poor. What should I do?
faqs.answer: If you're scanning or copying a photograph using EPSON Smart Panel, make sure you select Photo as your Scan Material or Document Type. If you're using EPSON TWAIN, select Color Photo (or Black & White Photo if your photo is black and white) as your Image Type. Adjust your Quality and Resolution settings. If you're using the automatic document feeder, try cleaning the paper path guide. Follow the instructions in "Cleaning the Paper Path Guide" on page 121 of your user's manual. If you're copying a photograph, use the EPSON Photo Paper in your Media Pack.

faqs.question: The image is faint or out of focus. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure the original document is placed flat on the document table. Check the condition of your original. If the document is damaged, dirty, or wrinkled, these imperfections will show up in your scan or copy. Adjust the Gamma and Exposure settings in your EPSON TWAIN software.

faqs.question: Straight lines in the image appear jagged. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure the edges of your original document are carefully aligned with the scales on the sides of the document table.

faqs.question: I'm having problems installing the software. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure your EPSON Stylus Scan is plugged in and turned on. Make sure you've closed all other applications, including any screen savers and anti-virus programs running in the background. Then try installing the software again, taking care to follow the instructions on the Start Here sheet.

faqs.question: How can I determine if there is a problem in the computer or the product?
faqs.answer:
You can run a printer check to determine whether the problem comes from the EPSON Stylus Scan or your computer.
1. Make sure both the EPSON Stylus Scan and your computer are turned off.
2. Disconnect the interface cable from the EPSON Stylus Scan.
3. Make sure paper is loaded.
4. Hold down the load/eject button, then press and release the Operate button. Continue holding down the load/eject button until the Operate light starts to flash, then release it. A check page is printed, showing the ROM version number, ink counter, and a nozzle check pattern.
5. After the page is printed, turn off the power. Then reconnect the interface cable and turn on your EPSON Stylus Scan and computer. If the results are satisfactory, the problem lies in your software settings, the interface cable, or your computer. If the check page does not print correctly, you may have a problem with your EPSON Stylus Scan. Try the suggestions in "Problems and Solutions" on page 139 of your user's manual for more information.

faqs.question: How should I transport my product?
faqs.answer:
For short moves, you can just pick up the EPSON Stylus Scan 2500 Pro by the handles on the side and set it down. For longer moves, you need to repack it in its original box and lock the print head and transportation lock. Do the following:
1. Turn on the EPSON Stylus Scan and wait until the print head locks in position. Then turn off the EPSON Stylus Scan.
2. Unplug the power cord, and then disconnect the interface cable.
3. Open the document and maintenance covers.
4. Push the transportation lock right (as you are facing the printer) to lock the scanner carriage.
5. Close the maintenance and document covers.
6. Remove all paper from the sheet feeder, and then remove the paper support.
7. Push in the output tray extension. Caution: To avoid damage, always leave the ink cartridges installed when transporting the EPSON Stylus Scan. Also, remember to lock the print head and the transportation lock. Push in the output tray extension. Lock the transportation lock. Note: Tape the print head to the right side from the front of the printer.
8. Use tape to secure the document cover. Secure the ink cartridge holder to the printer with tape.
9. Use the original box and packing materials to repack the EPSON Stylus Scan.
10. Keep the EPSON Stylus Scan level during transport. Caution: Be sure to remove the tape used in step 8 before printing.

faqs.question: Only the Operate light is on, but nothing prints. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Turn off the EPSON Stylus Scan and your computer. Make sure the interface cable is connected securely. (Use a fully shielded USB "AB" interface cable or an IEEE-1284 compliant parallel cable.) Make sure there's no packing material inside the EPSON Stylus Scan. Run a printer check as described on page 137. If you ran a printer check successfully, make sure your EPSON Stylus Scan and application software are installed correctly. If you're printing on a network, you may need to set up your EPSON Stylus Scan for network printing, as described in your electronic EPSON Stylus Scan 2500 Pro Reference Guide.

faqs.question: I try to copy on a Mac and the original is scanned but doesn't print. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Open the Chooser, select SS 2500, and turn on background printing. Then try copying again.

faqs.question: The Operate light does not turn on. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Make sure the power cable is correctly plugged into the EPSON Stylus Scan and the power outlet. Make sure the outlet is operational and is not connected to a timer or switch.
